evidence.paraphrase: The article motivates a measure that distinguishes the persistent state of wage growth from volatile worker-level observations and sector-specific noise.
Worker-level wage changes are combined with time-series filtering to estimate a persistent wage-inflation trend and its uncertainty interval.
The latent trend is decomposed into an economy-wide component and industry components so broad labor-cost pressure can be separated from sectoral reallocation.
The estimate is surrounded by a sixty-eight percent uncertainty band and can be affected by missing or disrupted source months, so point movements must not be overinterpreted.

executive_summary: The New York Fed Trend Wage Inflation framework decomposes worker-level wage growth into persistent and transitory movements and into economy-wide versus industry-specific components. For MacroTrace it is a latent-state labor-cost node with explicit uncertainty and sector heterogeneity, not a single observed wage-growth series or an unconditional claim about future price inflation.

method_routes.aggregation_role: labor-cost pressure factor with common and sector-specific evidence kept separately visible
method_routes.estimand: persistent common and industry-specific components of observed worker-level wage growth as of each vintage
method_routes.formula: wage_{i,s,t}=common_t+industry_{s,t}+transitory_{i,s,t}; latent states follow registered transition equations
method_routes.identification_strategy: time-series persistence and cross-industry covariance distinguish common trend, sector trends, and transitory noise
identifying_assumptions: worker observations are comparable over time after registered sample controls
latent-state dynamics are stable enough for filtering
missing observations are handled using only information available at the as-of date
method_routes.sample_definition: worker wage observations and industry assignments available in each monthly real-time vintage

questions.horizon_text: current latent wage trend and near-term persistence
questions.question_text: What portion of current U.S. wage inflation is persistent and common across industries, and what portion is transitory or industry specific?
